Overarching parent for the regional Bronze Age eras, which happened at meaningfully different times in different places -- spans from the start of the European Bronze Age (~-3,200) to the end of the East Asian Bronze Age (~-1,046). See ONTOLOGY.md's "Overarching regional eras for genuinely cross-regional themes". The geography.historical_regions field (formerly just east_asia) was removed 2026-08-31 -- a leftover from the demoted east_asian_bronze_age_era child that wrongly narrowed geography_matches to East Asia only (every other overarching era -- neolithic_era, paleolithic_era, classical_antiquity_era, iron_age_era, copper_age_era -- correctly has none at all, falling back to continent-level matching); this blocked Indus Valley Civilization's linked_era_id seed value, among others.

Overarching parent for the regional Classical Antiquity eras (mediterranean_classical_era, east_asian_classical_era, south_asian_classical_era, mesoamerican_formative_classic_era, andean_early_civilizations_era), which happened at meaningfully different times in different places -- same "overarching regional era" treatment as bronze_age_era/neolithic_era/ paleolithic_era/iron_age_era. Spans from the earliest regional start (-1200, shared by Mediterranean/Mesoamerican/Andean) to the latest regional end (900, Mesoamerican). Deliberately excludes Sub-Saharan Africa, whose equivalent-period record is iron_age_era, not a "classical antiquity" -- see ONTOLOGY.md's "Overarching regional eras for genuinely cross-regional themes" and STATUS.md.

The Chalcolithic/Copper Age transitional period between the Neolithic and the Bronze Age (Bronze Age itself starts -3200, where this ends -- see bronze_age_era). Added 2026-08-31 as a new overarching regional_era, same treatment as bronze_age_era/neolithic_era/paleolithic_era, but currently has no regional period records nested under it via broader_periods -- unlike those three, no Copper Age-specific period (e.g. a Fertile Crescent or European Chalcolithic record) exists yet in this dataset to link. Flagged in ROADMAP.md as follow-up work rather than fabricated here without a real source record.

Editorial navigation chapter. The Neolithic transition happened at very different times on different continents (roughly 10,000 BCE in the Fertile Crescent, much later in the Americas) -- this chapter's dates are a global envelope, not a claim of simultaneity. Editorial navigation chapter. Covers the Iron Age plus the classical and early imperial civilizations of the Mediterranean, Persia, India, and China, through the fall of the Western Roman Empire.

Editorial navigation chapter, 1945-present. end=2100 is schema.py's YEAR_MAX ceiling standing in for "open present" -- Period.end is required (unlike Polity.end), so an explicit far-future value is the least surprising way to represent "still ongoing." Editorial navigation chapter, not a claim that every society developed identically. Start is an open lower bound (earliest known stone tools keep pushing backward as of 2026); -3,000,000 is a round, citable ballpark (Lomekwian/Oldowan toolmaking), not a precise date. Empty continents list means deliberately global -- valid only at tier=macro_chapter, see ONTOLOGY.md. Dates use astronomical year numbering (year 0 exists), inherited from Wikidata via pipeline/wd_to_yaml.py's parse_year().

Late Bronze Age Greek civilization; Linear B gives economic records but no historiography, hence protohistorical. No matching polities/ record -- power was distributed across palace-centers (Mycenae, Pylos, Tiryns...), not a single political actor.

Overarching parent for the regional agricultural-transition eras, which happened at meaningfully different times, and under different technology packages, in different places -- spans from the Fertile Crescent's earliest agriculture (~-10,000) to the end of Neolithic Europe (~-1,700). Named "Neolithic & Archaic" rather than just "Neolithic" because the Americas' agricultural transition (mesoamerican_archaic_era, andean_archaic_era) is conventionally called "Archaic" in Americanist archaeology, not "Neolithic" -- a real terminology difference (different domesticates, no draft animals, a different technology trajectory than the Old World package), not just a regional relabeling of the same thing. See ONTOLOGY.md's "Overarching regional eras for genuinely cross-regional themes."
Pre-dynastic Egyptian and Nubian farming cultures.
